comment: Shared payout-estimate table for the Lead Globe research card. There are no public per-business market rates. The only public figure is the data licensing company's advertised range for company data, $100K–$5M, which also appears on Robert's invite page and in the short 'At a glance' block in config/scripts.json. Those scripts must keep citing that advertised envelope — not these per-category sub-ranges. Per-category estimates are for the in-app card (and an optional list chip) only. Never copy them into outreach email drafts, the landing page, or the opt-out page. They are not offers; only the data licensing company makes an offer.
methodology: Each category is placed in a wide sub-range inside the advertised $100K–$5M envelope, based on how data-rich that kind of business typically is: (1) how many core systems it tends to run (CRM, accounting, field service / operations, email and related tools), (2) how many years of records those systems often hold, and (3) typical record volume (jobs, invoices, tickets, transactions). This tool does not know a given company's actual systems, years, or volume, so the bands stay wide on purpose and are labeled as rough estimates by business type. No public per-business comps exist; the advertised range is the only published dollar figure used. Lower bands are for types that usually have fewer operational systems or thinner history (for example small single-location retail). Higher bands are for types that typically run several connected systems with years of operational records (multi-system trades and field service, dealerships, healthcare). Unknown types use the full advertised envelope as the default, rather than inventing a tighter range.

advertised.label: $100K–$5M
advertised.source: The data licensing company's advertised range for company data, also shown on https://robertwalker.dataearns.com/invite and in the 'At a glance' block in config/scripts.json.

caveat: Your estimate by business type, within the licensing company's advertised $100K–$5M range. Not an offer; only the data licensing company makes an offer.

tiers.label: Photo / video studio
tiers.rationale: Studios typically keep project files, images or video, and email, but fewer long-running operational systems (no field-service or ERP stack at scale) and lower record volume than trades, fleets, or clinical practices.

tiers.label: Agencies
tiers.rationale: Usually project files, briefs, creative, and client email rather than years of request-to-invoice operational systems. System count and volume are typically lighter than field service or dealership stacks.

tiers.label: Retail / e-commerce
tiers.rationale: Small single-location retail sits at the low end of the advertised envelope. Transaction, catalog, and ticket volume can be higher for larger or e-commerce operators, but this tool cannot see store count or years, so the band stays toward the lower advertised range.

tiers.label: Insurance
tiers.rationale: Policy, CRM, and claims files can be structured and long-lived, but book size is unknown here. Mid-low to mid band inside the advertised range. (Outreach to this category remains deferred; the estimate is for the research card only.)

tiers.label: Accounting firm
tiers.rationale: Document-heavy, with multi-year client files and collaboration tools. The licensing company's accounting ads mention firms with 10+ employees. Volume varies widely with firm size, so the band is mid-wide.

tiers.label: App / SaaS
tiers.rationale: Support tickets, product documentation, and operations logs can span several systems, but years and volume vary a lot by product, so this sits in a mid band.

tiers.label: Call center / BPO
tiers.rationale: Established centers can hold high ticket, chat, and call volume. They often have fewer job-to-invoice operational systems than trades, so the band is mid rather than at the top of the advertised range.

tiers.label: Property management
tiers.rationale: Typically several connected systems (property, work-order, accounting, and email) and years of maintenance and resident-service records. Mid band; portfolio size is unknown.

tiers.label: Logistics / fleet
tiers.rationale: Dispatch, shipment, fleet maintenance, and operations systems usually run together and accumulate ongoing volume. Years and fleet size are unknown, so the band is mid to mid-high.

tiers.label: Contractors
tiers.rationale: Bids, change orders, job logs, project documents, and accounting — often multi-system when the firm is established. Not always as field-service-system-heavy as dedicated home-services trades, so the band starts slightly lower than that tier.

tiers.label: Home services
tiers.rationale: Multi-system trades and field service typically run CRM or field-service software plus accounting and email, with years of request, quote, job, and invoice records. That pattern is data-richer than single-location retail, so this tier sits higher in the advertised envelope.

tiers.label: Auto dealer / auto group
tiers.rationale: Dealerships typically run a DMS or CRM, sales, and service-order systems with high customer and repair volume, so they sit in the upper half of the advertised range. This extract label can also include auto-repair and tyre shops, which may be thinner than a full dealer group; the band is wide for that reason.

tiers.label: Manufacturer
tiers.rationale: Work orders, ERP records, and quality logs usually mean several operational systems and years of production history. The licensing company's manufacturer ads do not state a company size, so the band stays wide in the upper half.

tiers.label: Medical / dental
tiers.rationale: Clinical, scheduling, billing, and communications systems typically hold long histories and high record volume, so healthcare sits toward the top of the advertised envelope. (Outreach to this category remains deferred; the estimate is for the research card only.)

tiers.label: Oil & gas
tiers.rationale: Well logs, field reports, and maintenance records are specialized, often long-lived operational data. Ads for this type do not state a company size. Upper bound is the advertised cap.

tiers.label: General / unknown type
tiers.rationale: Fallback when the business type is unknown or unmapped. With no category signal, the estimate is the full advertised $100K–$5M envelope rather than a tighter invented band.
